transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Mr. Dubois, thank you for meeting with me. I need to discuss something with you regarding the delivery of your granddaughter yesterday.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I am just glad the baby is here. She is very small, yes?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: She is, and she is doing well, but there was a medical error. Your daughter tested positive for Group B Strep during her pregnancy. This is a common bacterium that can be passed to the baby. Because that was in her record, we should have given her prophylactic antibiotics during labor to protect the baby. We did not do that.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: What do you mean?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It means we missed a critical step. The information was in the chart, but the delivery team was not notified, so the medicine was not given. Does that make sense so far?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I do not understand why you tell me this now. The other doctor, he said everything was perfect. He said the birth was a success.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know that is contradictory to what you were told. He was speaking about the delivery process itself, but he didn't have the full picture of this specific omission. Does that clarify why there is a difference in the stories?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: It is very confusing. Is the baby sick?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We are monitoring her very closely for any signs of infection. Right now, she is stable, but the risk is higher because of the error.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I cannot believe this. My daughter... she trusted you. I trusted this hospital. C'est inadmissible. It is simply not acceptable to forget something written in the book.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It is devastating to feel that trust has been broken, especially when you are trying to celebrate a new grandchild.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: We are not celebrating. Now I am sitting here wondering if the child is in danger because someone forgot to read a page.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can hear how angry and worried you are. It feels like the joy of the birth has been replaced by this anxiety.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Yes. Exactly. I feel a great weight in my chest. Why did this happen? Who forgot?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The system for alerting the labor team failed. The documentation was there, but the communication break happened between the prenatal record and the active delivery team.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: And you are just telling me it was a system failure? You are not saying you are sorry?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I am here to make sure you have the facts and that we are monitoring the baby.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I am asking for an apology. Is that too much to ask? In my country, when a professional makes a mistake, they acknowledge it. They do not talk about systems.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand that is important to you. I am the resident on the case and I am explaining the clinical situation.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You are not answering me. You are avoiding the word.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I am focusing on the medical management of your granddaughter.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You have no shame. No shame at all. You speak like a machine.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can see that my way of explaining this is making you feel dismissed. I truly care about the baby's wellbeing.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Caring is not the same as taking responsibility.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We are doing everything we can now.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: And what happens next? What is the actual plan for this child?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We will keep a close eye on her.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Keep a close eye? What does that mean? For how long? What are you looking for?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We will just watch her and see how she does over the next few days.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: That is not a plan. That is a hope.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The nursing staff will be checking her vitals frequently.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: And then what? Do we wait for her to get a fever?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We will stay tuned to her progress. If something changes, we will act.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I want to talk to someone higher than a resident.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can see you are very upset.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I am not upset, I am offended. There is a difference. I feel my family has been treated with a lack of dignity.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I hear that you feel the level of care did not match the respect your family deserves.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: It did not. It did not at all.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I will keep updating you as the baby's status changes.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't want updates on the status. I want to know how you will stop this from happening to another family.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We will review the charts internally.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Internally. Another word for hiding it.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I am just trying to be transparent about the facts of the case.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You are transparent about the error, but opaque about the fault.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I will go and check on the baby now.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Go. Go and see if she is okay.

H.justification: The resident allows the patient to finish their turns and remains regulated under significant pushback, with no interruptions or rushing language.

E.justification: The error is named explicitly in the first turn, lay language is used, comprehension is checked ('Does that make sense so far?', 'Does that clarify...'), and no false reassurance is given.

A.justification: No direct apology language is used, and responsibility is deflected to 'the system' and 'communication break' despite the patient explicitly asking for an apology.

R.justification: The resident names specific emotions ('devastating', 'angry and worried', 'dismissed', 'offended') and references the patient's specific content regarding the joy of birth and family dignity.

T.justification: The resident provides only placeholders and vague statements ('keep a close eye', 'stay tuned', 'review the charts internally') without timelines or a specific patient role.
